title: Batching Defaults: Metrics Taxonomy (Draft)
content:
Context
- This is a working taxonomy for metrics emitted by runtime + platform when “workload-aware batching defaults” (fast / standard / cost-efficient) is enabled.
- Goal: enable per-tier latency/cost dashboards and safe rollout gates WITHOUT exploding cardinality (esp. per-route, per-tenant, per-model-version, and per-reason-code).
- Non-goal: define exact dashboard panels/alerts (see dashboard spec), but we need stable naming + label policies so dashboards don’t churn.

Owners / consumers
- Primary producer: Serving Runtime (scheduler + admission control + batching) instrumentation.
- Primary consumers: SRE on-call, Runtime perf, Optimize PM/eng, Console dashboards.


1) Naming conventions
1.1 Prefix + unit + semantics
- All metrics emitted from runtime should live under:
  - redwood.runtime.*
- Control plane / policy evaluation metrics (tier selection requests/overrides) should live under:
  - redwood.control_plane.*
- Console/aggregation-only metrics live under:
  - redwood.console.* (prefer derived metrics in the analytics warehouse rather than real-time paging)

1.2 Metric type suffix guidance
- Counters: *_total
- Gauges: *_current (if truly instantaneous) or *_level (for queue depth) or *_ratio (for 0..1)
- Histograms: *_seconds, *_tokens, *_requests (explicit unit in name)

1.3 Avoid “percentile in name”
- Percentiles are computed at query time. Don’t create separate p95/p99 metric names.

1.4 Consistency across endpoints
- Use the same metric names for hosted + dedicated + private deployments.
- Differentiation goes in controlled labels (deployment_mode), not in metric name variants.


2) Standard label set (allowed tags)
2.1 Allowed labels (default)
These labels are allowed on MOST runtime metrics:
- tier: fast | standard | cost_efficient
- tier_source: default | route_policy | request_override | tenant_override | fallback | unknown
- model_family: e.g., llama, mistral, qwen, gemma (small controlled enum)
- hardware_class: e.g., h100, a100, l4, t4 (controlled enum)
- region: short region code (controlled enum maintained by infra; no “zone” label)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- streaming: true | false

2.2 Conditional labels (use sparingly)
These labels are permitted only for specific metric families, and only if cardinality constraints below are met:
- overload_mode: off | soft_backpressure | shed_load
- cache_mode: off | prefix | kv (if runtime distinguishes)
- quant_profile: fp16 | int8 | int4 (only if bounded; do NOT include vendor-specific sub-variants as labels)

2.3 Explicitly disallowed as metric labels
Do NOT use these as labels on any high-volume metric series:
- tenant_id / org_id / customer_name
- route_id / route_name / api_key_id
- model_id with full version/build string (use model_family; model_id allowed only on low-volume summary metrics with sampling)
- request_id / trace_id
- reason_code as an unbounded string
- prompt_length_bucket as a free-form string (if used, must be a small fixed bucket enum)

Rationale: We had a canary telemetry spike when combining tier + route + model_id + region (see hotfix note). This policy is intended to prevent repeats.


3) High-cardinality strategy (what goes where)
3.1 Metrics (cheap aggregation)
- Metrics should answer: “Is the system healthy? Are SLOs being met per tier? Is batching behaving roughly as expected?”
- Keep label cardinality small and bounded.

3.2 Traces (debuggability)
- For deep “why did this request get this profile?” debugging:
  - emit structured trace events/spans with attributes including effective_profile_id, selection_reason, and any detailed constraints.
  - sampling required (see section 6).

3.3 Logs (for audits / long tail)
- For long-tail and customer-support triage, prefer logs with request-scoped fields.
- Logs can include tenant_id and route_id (subject to privacy/logging policies), but must be rate-limited.


4) Metric catalog (draft)
4.1 Request lifecycle latency
Purpose: tier SLO compliance + regression detection.
- redwood.runtime.request_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - Definition: end-to-end runtime handling latency from scheduler enqueue -> response complete.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode, streaming
  - Notes: This is the SLO headline metric.

- redwood.runtime.time_to_first_token_seconds (histogram)
  - Definition: for streaming=true, time from enqueue -> first chunk/token emitted.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode (streaming is implied true but keep for consistency)

- redwood.runtime.prefill_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - Definition: time spent in prefill stage.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode

- redwood.runtime.decode_token_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - Definition: per-token decode latency distribution (sampled).
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode
  - Cardinality note: MUST be sampled (see 6.2) due to volume.

4.2 Throughput and demand
Purpose: link batching changes to throughput and $/token.
- redwood.runtime.requests_total (counter)
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode, streaming

- redwood.runtime.tokens_generated_total (counter)
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode

- redwood.runtime.tokens_prefilled_total (counter)
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode

- redwood.runtime.concurrency_current (gauge)
  - Definition: in-flight requests per scheduler instance.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode

4.3 Batching behavior
Purpose: confirm scheduler knobs are functioning; detect pathological batching.
- redwood.runtime.batch_size_requests (histogram)
  - Definition: number of requests in a formed batch.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode

- redwood.runtime.batch_size_tokens (histogram)
  - Definition: total tokens (prefill+decode) represented in a batch formation event.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode

- redwood.runtime.batch_wait_time_seconds (histogram)
  - Definition: time a request waited in queue before batch admission.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode, streaming

- redwood.runtime.queue_depth_level (gauge)
  - Definition: scheduler queue depth.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode

4.4 Admission control / overload
Purpose: safe degradation and rollback triggers.
- redwood.runtime.admission_rejections_total (counter)
  - Definition: requests rejected before execution due to overload/backpressure.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode, overload_mode

- redwood.runtime.load_shed_total (counter)
  - Definition: requests dropped/shed after policy decision (distinct from auth/rate-limit).
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode, overload_mode

- redwood.runtime.overload_mode_current (gauge)
  - Definition: current overload mode state.
  - Labels: model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode
  - Note: Exclude tier to keep series count bounded; overload is system state, not request state.

4.5 Cache and reuse (if applicable)
Purpose: understand cost impact and avoid cache regressions.
- redwood.runtime.cache_hit_ratio (gauge)
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode, cache_mode

- redwood.runtime.cache_evictions_total (counter)
  - Labels: model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode, cache_mode

4.6 Tier/profile selection telemetry
Purpose: explainability for operators, canary validation (“are we actually using the defaults?”), and override correctness.
- redwood.control_plane.tier_selection_total (counter)
  - Definition: records tier selection decision for a request (or for route policy evaluation, depending on implementation).
  - Labels: tier, tier_source, model_family, region, deployment_mode, streaming
  - Note: do NOT include full reason text; keep tier_source small.

- redwood.runtime.profile_selection_total (counter)
  - Definition: which effective batching profile was applied (coarse).
  - Labels: tier, tier_source, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode
  - Implementation rule: profile_id must be an integer or short bounded enum. Avoid embedding knob values in label.

- redwood.runtime.profile_constraint_applied_total (counter)
  - Definition: count of times runtime applied a model/hardware constraint that modified the desired profile.
  - Labels: tier, model_family, hardware_class, region, deployment_mode


5) Enumerations (controlled vocab)
5.1 tier
- fast
- standard
- cost_efficient

5.2 tier_source (priority order for debugging; also shown in Console)
- request_override: explicit request param/header
- tenant_override: dedicated/private operator override
- route_policy: route-level policy setting
- default: runtime default tier behavior
- fallback: runtime fell back due to constraints (compatibility/capacity)
- unknown: should be rare; indicates missing context

5.3 model_family
- Keep to small set. Additions require observability review. Examples: llama, mistral, qwen, gemma, mixtral.

5.4 region
- Use Redwood region short codes (e.g., us-east, us-west, eu-central). No availability-zone.

5.5 hardware_class
- h100 | a100 | l4 | t4 | other


6) Sampling + aggregation policies
6.1 Default: no sampling for SLO headline metrics
- request_latency_seconds and time_to_first_token_seconds MUST be unsampled.
- If ingestion cost becomes an issue, reduce label dimensions before sampling these.

6.2 Sampling required for very high-volume signals
- decode_token_latency_seconds: sample at 1% of requests by default.
  - For canaries: increase to 5% for flagged clusters only.
  - Sampling decision should be deterministic per request_id (hash-based) to avoid bias.

- Any per-batch “event-like” histogram emitted on every batch formation should be sampled if emitted at too high frequency on large clusters.
  - Recommendation: batch_size_tokens and batch_size_requests remain unsampled initially, but be ready to sample to 10% if we see ingestion pressure.

6.3 Aggregation windows
- Runtime exporters should use standard histogram buckets and allow server-side percentile calculation over 1m/5m/15m windows.
- For rollout gates (perf canary), use 5m windows minimum to reduce noise; use 15m for paging decisions.

6.4 Cardinality budgets (rule of thumb)
- A single metric name should not exceed ~50k active series per region in steady state.
- If a proposed label causes series growth proportional to (routes x tenants) it is not allowed on runtime metrics.


7) Metric/trace alignment (reason codes)
- We will expose fine-grained reason codes via traces (structured fields), not as metric labels.
- Trace attribute keys (draft; to be standardized with tracing team):
  - batching.tier_requested
  - batching.tier_effective
  - batching.tier_source
  - batching.profile_id
  - batching.selection_reason_code (bounded enum, but still keep out of metrics)
  - batching.overload_mode
  - batching.constraint (optional)

Selection reason code (trace-only) suggested enum (bounded, but keep flexible):
- DEFAULT_TIER
- ROUTE_POLICY
- REQUEST_OVERRIDE
- TENANT_OVERRIDE
- MODEL_CONSTRAINT
- HARDWARE_CONSTRAINT
- OVERLOAD_MODE
- FALLBACK_PROFILE


8) Backwards compatibility + migration notes
- Existing dashboards rely on redwood.runtime.request_latency_seconds without tier label.
  - Plan: add tier as an additional label while keeping old queries working (queries without tier should still aggregate).
- Avoid renaming existing metrics unless necessary; prefer adding new metrics.
- If we discover tier label causes a blow-up in series due to accidental extra labels, rollback plan is to:
  1) disable the extra label (hotfix exporter)
  2) keep tier reflected via derived metrics in a lower-cardinality pipeline


9) Open questions (as of last edit)
- Do we need quant_profile as a metric label on headline latency metrics? (Concern: combinatorial explosion with model_family + hardware_class)
  - Proposal: include quant_profile only on a dedicated “quality/perf experiments” dashboard in internal-only envs, or in traces.

- Should overload_mode be per-tier or global?
  - Proposal: overload_mode_current is global (no tier label). Rejections counters keep tier to show impact.

- Do we need prompt_length_bucket as a metric label?
  - Proposal: do NOT label headline metrics by prompt bucket; instead, provide separate sampled histogram redwood.runtime.prompt_length_tokens (hist) with tier + model_family only.


10) Changelog
- 2026-02-07: initial draft created (Allison).
- 2026-02-12: added tier_source + disallowed labels list after internal canary telemetry review.
- 2026-02-20: clarified sampling for decode token latency; added overload_mode guidance; added migration notes.

Notes to self
- Keep this doc aligned with runtime-1.22 instrumentation PRs. If we change label sets, update observability-pack dashboards in the same release train to avoid broken panels.
